name: Subdomain Takeover via Dangling CNAME
description: shop-old.acme.io still has a CNAME to a Heroku app that was deleted in 2021. An attacker registers the same Heroku app name, claims the dangling pointer, and starts serving a near-perfect phishing clone of the login page on a trusted-looking acme.io subdomain.
reasoning: The corporate edge serves the modern shop, while the dangling subdomain is now under attacker control. The simulation models the attacker-controlled shop-old.acme.io as a 'compromised' edge node that customers reach via legitimate links shared in social engineering email.

narrative.text: Quiet baseline. Modern shop sees normal diurnal traffic.
Bug-bounty researcher tweets a reachability test for shop-old.acme.io — 200 OK from Heroku app they just claimed.
Phishing wave begins; emails link to https://shop-old.acme.io/login (looks legit, valid TLS via Heroku-managed cert).
Attacker mirrors the login UI, harvests creds, then redirects to real /login to mask the theft.
auth-svc sees a small spike of 'logged in twice in 4s from different IPs' — suspicious sessions opened.
Customer support ticket flood mentions 'weird login page'. Brand-protection routes it to security.
DNS team deletes the dangling CNAME; cert revoked on the attacker app via Heroku abuse-contact.
All sessions opened from the phishing window force-logged out; password reset emails sent.
Steady state. Action item: external attack-surface scanner alert on dangling CNAMEs.
